problem: Calculate the sum \( S(z) \) of the power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n}(z-i)^n \) for \( z \) within the convergence disk.

answer_text:
Let

\[
w=z-i.
\]

Then the series becomes

\[
S(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n}w^n.
\]

The radius of convergence is

\[
R=\frac{1}{\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{(-1)^n}{n}\right|^{1/n}}=1,
\]

so the convergence disk is

\[
|z-i|<1.
\]

Recall the Maclaurin series

\[
\log(1+w)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{n+1}\frac{w^n}{n},\qquad |w|<1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^n\frac{w^n}{n}
=-\log(1+w).
\]

Substituting back \(w=z-i\), we get

\[
S(z)=-\log(1+z-i).
\]

Here \(\log\) denotes the branch analytic in the disk \(|z-i|<1\), for example the principal branch, since \(1+z-i\) stays in the right half-plane in that disk.

Thus,

\[
\boxed{S(z)=-\log(1+z-i)}
\]
